change: perf(engine) 7e32778f -- doc-generation budget scales to source-file count (<=3 files -> 90s, was 300s)
why: Measured on a graded hard-task build: 2.8 min of iteration work, 13.4 min wall clock, and 5.0 of those minutes were auto-documentation timing out at 300s while generating an eight-file architecture suite for a project containing one 20-line Python module.
confirmed_in_production: Real build log: 'Auto-documentation: 2 source file(s) -- capping generation at 90s (was 300s)' then 'timed out after 90s'. 210 seconds saved per build.
verdict: DIRECTIONAL, not certified. Median wall clock on the same graded task moved 12.8 -> 8.6 min. The mechanism is confirmed by the build log (a fixed 210s no longer spent), but n=2 before the change is too thin for a significance test, and the after-group spans 6.1-21.0 min because it includes the stripped-prompt arm's non-converging runs.
not_claimed: No multiplier. The saving is a CAP on wasted time, not a speedup of the build itself: iteration work was unchanged at ~2.4-2.8 min. A project with more than 3 source files keeps the full 300s budget.
